facts.text: Brenus had ended the village's taxes, tithes and chores in exchange for a pint of blood from a resident once every moon.
In return for blood, the Vrakieri share drops of their cursed blood with commoners, curing plague and granting immunity to disease.
Under Brenis's rule, the only passage into Veil Sangora was sealed, preventing anyone from entering or leaving.
Most soldiers of Veil Sangora swore allegiance to Brenis and were forbidden from killing the human population, who were treated as valuable livestock.
Brenis banned all silver in Veil Sangora, punishable by death, because it can harm the Vrakieri.
The ruling Vrakhiri imposed an oppressive 'blood tax' on the human peasantry.
The story begins in the year 1347, during the Black Death pandemic sweeping across Europe.
Cohen and Lacra learned that something beneath Svatra leaks Anahora's dark power into the world, and Brenis intends to seize control of it through a ritual completed at his coronation.
The 14th century setting of The Blood of Dawnwalker is marked by collapse, plague, and widespread death across Europe.
Drinking Ambress's blood pulled Cohen's consciousness into Anahora, the dimension from which the corruption creating Verkieri originated and where Verkieri souls go after death.
Interrupting the ritual causes the barrier between Anahora and reality to partially collapse around Griefberg instead of closing cleanly, turning the castle into a supernatural disaster zone.
After the ritual's disruption, corpses rise, spectral entities appear, parts of the castle are torn upward, and living prisoners appear possessed by forces from Anahora.
The Blood of Dawnwalker is set in 14th century medieval Europe, in a region called Vale Sangora within the Carpathian area.
Vrakhiri are ancient, true-born or noble vampires known for high intelligence and immense power.
Knyaz and Boyars are medieval political titles given to vampire lords who rule over territories.
Murohns, also called Murons, are feral, mindless, bloodthirsty monstrosities created when a vampire's transformation into a Vrakieri fails or is performed imprecisely.
A Vrakieri is created when another Vrakieri pierces a human's heart with one of their fangs.
Vrakieri do not age and heal from wounds almost instantly.
Vrakieri are not harmed by crucifixes or garlic, but silver and sunlight pose a genuine threat to them.
Vrakieri need human blood to survive.

Anahora is ruled by a nameless entity that Verkieri fear more than humans fear Satan; after death, Verkieri souls wander cursed plains under its gaze. The Sanjani refused to discuss this entity, saying they feared it more than any earthly creature.
Lacra explained that the force which turns humans into Verkieri and Moroni is a form of corruption, not ordinary magic, and it can also affect animals and plants.
A Vraker's body normally crumbles to dust after death, making Kalas's preserved fused form unusual.
Lakra explains that a Mandre can grow when a powerful Vraker's remains, such as ashes or teeth, stay in one place for centuries.
Xanthe warns Coen the Dawnwalker that he does not understand what truly lies beneath the city or what Brennes is doing there.
In ancient Rome, a laurel crown (bay leaf wreath) was a symbol of triumph and victory worn by victorious generals and emperors.
The tradition of wearing laurel crowns originated in Greek mythology and was later adopted by the Romans.
Inside the cave, Cohen found an ancient tomb of a great warrior woman who fought the Vrakieri long ago and chose to burn herself rather than be turned into one.
Anka was expelled from St. Tina's Convent by Mother Superior Bernice after Leonica betrayed her by reporting her interest in magic.
Vulk and Pieta had been mercenaries together, fighting in Ireland, Constantinople, and for the King of France.
Pieta retired from mercenary life about 20 years earlier after the Battle of Cassell.
Vulk was captured and tortured five years before the story, losing his eyes, before eventually finding Pieta in Veil Sangora.
A monk at Marrair Monastery revealed that Pieta had donated all his gold to build a scriptorium, seeking atonement for burning the city of Cassell and its people.

Anka discovered a hidden forbidden library at St. Tina's Convent and shared it with her friend Leonica (also called Omnia/Yonica/Leonuka); after praying unsuccessfully for God to save the convent from the plague ravaging it, Leonica turned to the forbidden manuscripts and bargained with a dark entity with burning eyes and tentacles to try to save the convent.
Pilgrims at St. Tina's Convent tore apart the corpse of Saint Tina hoping her relics would cure the plague, but it failed.
Some nuns sacrificed themselves to hide fragments of Saint Tina's relics; those killed by pilgrims rather than plague did not rise as undead.
Leonica's bargain resulted in the infected nuns being cursed to rot alive without dying, their souls trapped in decaying bodies.
Kinyaz Scender Dragosti ruled Veil Sangora, having taken the throne in 1324 after his father died in a hunting accident.

Within Isbrand's memories, Cohen and Lacra witnessed that Brenis was once a Roman legion commander whose army was defeated in battle, after which he and survivors fled into a place haunted by otherworldly shadows.
In a memory, Isbrand is revealed to have been a Roman military commander before being turned into a vampire over ten centuries before the present day.
Brencis's family owned a vast landed estate in ancient Rome, complete with slaves, placing them among the wealthiest of the Roman elite.
Xanthe was once a high priestess on a remote Greek island in antiquity.
Isbrand confronted the sole-surviving Brenis and offered him a choice: kneel and become a Verkieri, or die; Brenis chose to become a Verkieri.
Bakir was originally a warrior of the Central Asian steppes, among the Huns, who pillaged across Eurasia centuries ago.
After nine years of oppression, the people of Veil Sangora rose against Kinyaz Scender Dragosti.

After his transformation, Brenis returned to his estate, where Isbrand made him kill the guards who refused entry and confront his wife Helvia; Helvia (in some accounts described instead as Isbrand's wife) did not recognize him and burned herself alive rather than go with him, severing his ties to his former life.
Kinyaz Scender Dragosti crushed the uprising at Shrikes Crag, massacring the peasants and leaving no survivors.
Bakir recounts that in his first life he served as advisor to the Kagan of the Ruran tribe.
Brencis was born in 131 AD, during what is considered the golden era of the Roman Empire, under the name Caeso Burrienus Laurentius.
On a full moon night in 1347, a peasant named Cohen fled with his dying sister Luca from soldiers of Kinyaz Scender Dragosti who were ordered to kill anyone showing signs of plague infection.
Cohen and Luca were cornered by soldiers among the ruins of an old church.
Catalin's father Scander previously ruled Veil Sangora before the Verkieri under Brenis took power.
Four vampires called Vrakieri, led by Brenis, ambushed and killed Kinyaz Scender Dragosti's soldiers at the church.
Cohen begged Brenis to save his dying sister Luca, and Brenis healed her plague symptoms by giving her some of his tainted blood.
The Vrakieri drained Kinyaz Scender Dragosti of all his blood as he begged for mercy, killing him.
That same night, Brenis and his three boyers, Ambress, Bakir, and Zanthy, seized control of Veil Sangora.
Brenis and his boyers slaughtered most of the local nobility, turning some into blood donors and others into court jesters.
Isbrand becomes empowered by a mysterious force at a certain place, gaining power he claims Lacra could have shared had she stayed loyal.
Brenis abolished all taxes except the blood tithe owed to the Vrakieri rulers.
After the Vrakieri takeover, Brenis invited the Uryashi into his service, and many left their mountain villages to serve him.
Vladimir conspired with men from Svatra to rise up against the vampire lord Brenus.
By 1349, two years after the Vrakieri takeover, the mining village of Lazla still had to pay the blood tithe.
Esme became too weak to attend the blood mass, putting her at risk of being deemed worthless and killed by the Vrakieri.
Cohen's father Pieta sent him to the village herbalist Anka for a tonic to help Esme.
While fishing with his siblings Jana, Lunka, and Meto, Cohen was confronted by one of Brenis's soldiers asking about Pieta.
An Uryashi commander intervened to stop the soldier from threatening Cohen's sister Jana.
Cohen found his father Pieta arguing with neighbor Vladimir about time running out for a secret plan.
Vladimir asked Pieta to lead the men of Lazla to an abandoned silver mine to extract silver, which harms the Vrakieri.
Cohen discovered that Lazar had been killed inside a cave after fleeing a wolf attack, and someone had murdered him there deliberately.
Vladimir told Cohen the resistance planned to attack the silver mine while Brenis was away, with approval from resistance leader Craig.
Brenis singled out the weakened Esme at the blood mass, calling her a sickly sheep to be culled, prompting Cohen to publicly call him a monster.
Pieta decided to lead the miners in a defense of the silver mine after realizing Esme's death was otherwise inevitable.
Brenis's soldiers attacked the silver mine, having learned of the rebels' plan in advance.
During the mine battle, black mist and blood-red moths burst in and knocked Cohen unconscious.
Cohen, sensing blood from wounded miner Costl, lost control and bit him, feeding on his blood.

At the silver mine after the failed uprising, Brenis turned Cohen into a Vrakieri—tearing out one of his own fangs to pierce Cohen's heart (also described as feeding him vampiric blood)—sparing him at his father Pieta's plea instead of killing him.
Costl attacked the newly turned Cohen with a dagger, causing both to fall into a mineshaft.
Bakir was captured by enemies of the Kagan, tortured, and eventually managed to escape.
During the chaos of the Black Plague, high-ranking vampires known as Vrakhiri emerged from hiding and seized control of human settlements.

When the village rose against him, Brenis forced Pieta and Cohen to watch as he destroyed Lazla and took Cohen's family away, blaming Pieta for the resistance and calling Cohen a 'monster' for the uprising.
Brenis cut Pieta to tempt Cohen's bloodlust, but Cohen restrained himself and refused to kill his father.
Brenis defeated Cohen in battle and bit him, but Cohen's blood burned and weakened Brenis from within.
Brenis pinned Cohen to a tree with a pickaxe and left him to die at dawn, unable to understand why Cohen's blood harmed him.
The book Sancti Mihi Histori Vera reveals that Saint Mihi, believed by the valley's people to have fought dragons, actually fought the Verkieri.
According to the manuscript, Saint Mihi was a pagan who struck down a Verkier with a magically strengthened sword that cut through evil.
In Augusti, Cohen found the skeletons of Hila's parents in a house marked with a plague cross.
Tonis explained that Hila ran into the forest 10 years earlier while their father was beating their mother, and she never returned.
Isbrand punished Lacra, his progeny, for violating ancient vampire law—ordering Brenis to tear out her teeth, killing her companions, and banishing her from his presence.
Rosalia waited for letters from Ambrus after one of his military campaigns, but his replies stopped coming.
Rosalia wrote to Ambrus saying she planned to travel to Svartroad to learn what happened to him.
After the failed uprising, Lazla (Lazlia) was sacked and burned by Brenis's forces; its people were killed, taken, or disappeared without explanation, leaving only charred corpses.
Cohen survived being impaled and left in sunlight, later found alive by Anka who nursed him back to health.
Anka used necromantic magic to question a dead soldier, learning that the villagers of Lazla were taken to Brenis's castle dungeons for his coronation.
Brenis's coronation, where the captured villagers' blood would be used, was set to occur in 30 days.
Saint Mihi's body was believed lost, but the manuscript claims he was buried with his belongings somewhere in Svartra.
After escaping captivity, Bakir wandered the plains in a confused, half-mad state without purpose.
Cohen learned that the miller Mert was a member of the resistance group called the Manommits.
Mert was captured and imprisoned at Stonewood Post after being suspected of belonging to the rebel cell.
Cohen infiltrated Stonewood Post, freed Mert, and fought his way out after learning of a resistance meeting point.
Cohen rescued the rebel Sarah from Brenis's soldiers near a bridge, and she led him toward the Manommit camp.
Sarah led Cohen into an ambush by the Manommits, who captured him using a silver chain.
Manommit leader Craig was skeptical of Cohen but agreed to consider an alliance if Cohen kept disrupting Brenis's forces.

After Cohen defeated him, Saint Mihi revealed that Tobias—a monk who believed Mihi was a pagan sorcerer—had betrayed and imprisoned him underground centuries earlier, fabricating the church legend of St. Mihi despite the good Mihi had done.
When Ambrus stood up to Skender, Skender punished him by pouring boiling water down his throat and throwing him in a dungeon to die.
Rosalia eventually learned Ambrus had defied Skender and been imprisoned, and she wrote him a heartbroken letter believing she would never see him again.
Cohen and Vulk searched unsuccessfully for gold Pieta supposedly received from the King of France after the Battle of Cassell.
Cohen found cave drawings made by cobalts depicting Mihi as a monstrous warrior who slaughtered many cobalts before being defeated by a lone cobalt hero who shattered his sword.
When Brencis invaded Vale Sanguinar, he found Ambrus dying in Skender's dungeon.
Brencis offered Ambrus a choice: die, or be turned and serve Brencis as his new master.
After Cohen's visits, soldiers attacked Vulk's shack looking for Cohen, but Vulk killed them rather than betray him.
After being turned into a Vrakir, Ambrus wrote to Rosalia telling her he had been reborn with the gift of eternal life and asking her to meet him on the night of the full moon.
Ambrus intended to turn Rosalia into a Vrakir so they could live together forever.
Bakir was found and taken in by a being named Arachia, who turned him and also tortured him for pleasure.
Brencis survived for centuries hidden in the shadows before the 14th-century plague let him establish Vale Sangora as his personal domain.
Cohen raided Vrakieri boyer camps and caravans to disrupt their logistics and gain combat experience.
In the ruins beneath Svatra, Cohen and Lacra witnessed the final battle where Isbrand warned Brenis that beings called the Augurs would come for him for violating Verkieri law.
Three Boyars, Bakir, Ambress, and Zanthy, came to Brenis's aid, and together they managed to defeat Isbrand in the ruins beneath Svatra.
After Ambrus was turned, he and Brencis invaded Vale Sanguinar together, targeting the royal nobles first.
Ambrus and Brencis killed Skender and most of the other nobles of Vale Sanguinar during the invasion.
Ambrus attempted to turn Rosalia, but the transformation failed and she became a Moroi instead of a Vrakir.
Ambrus could not bring himself to kill Rosalia after she turned into a Moroi, so he abandoned her, leaving her violent and hungry for blood, with her old letters still on her body.
In the convent catacombs, Anka and Cohen found Leonica performing a blood ritual using occult symbols matching those on Anka's hands and Cohen's skin.

Cohen killed Leonica (Omnia/Leonuka) during her ritual on Anka's warning, stopping her when she was one step away from ending the convent's curse; afterward Cohen and Anka discovered notes revealing she had actually been trying to break the curse and free the cursed nuns' souls.
Brenis declared afterward that he had mastered the power seeping from the ruins beneath Svatra, which comes directly from Anahora.
Most nobles fought back against the invasion except Yulian Caudren, who knelt and kissed Ambrus's hand to pledge loyalty.

Feeling responsible for the tragedy, Anka performed the ritual herself alone in the catacombs (while Cohen waited in the library listening to inhuman sounds), freeing the cursed nuns' souls—who had already been dead for a long time—and afterward the undead nuns vanished.
Katnika eventually got her wish to be turned, but it was Bekir, not Ambrus, who turned her into a Moroi.
After roughly five years with Arachia, Bakir killed him, an act he describes as finally becoming a man instead of a pest.
Lacra told Cohen that long ago, near their current location, Saint Mihi fought an ancient Verkieri (Vraker) named Kalas, who could thin the veil between reality and Anahora.

Ambrus ordered that the noble Romulus, who loved hunting and mutilated peasants for poaching, be dismembered piece by piece for each animal trophy he owned, then stitched back together by his wife and displayed publicly.
Ambrus ordered that the noble Mycea, who whipped his serfs for minor offenses, be forced to whip himself continuously until he stopped, at which point he would be drawn and quartered.
Ambrus ordered that the noble Emanoil, who sold crops for gold while his peasants starved, have his melted valuables poured down his throat and his body denied burial.

Ambrus ordered that the noble Ion Borsa, who valued his hunting dogs and animals above his servants, be trampled by cows, doused in horse urine, and stuffed with sheep droppings before being displayed publicly.
Brencis is the mastermind who turned Coen into a Dawnwalker, intending to use him as an ultimate weapon or vessel.
Years before the main story, Cohen and his brother Alen disobeyed their father Pieta's warning and went onto thinning river ice; Alen fell through and drowned before help could save him.
Albertus devoted his life to studying the history of Veil Sangora, but the Verkieri banished him and destroyed his life's work when they seized power.
Farcus explained that Bakir killed most of his family but spared him and his brother Ducen, whom Bakir sexually abused and crippled after Ducen refused his advances.
Dr. Simeon researched the plague and tried to synthesize medicine from Verkier blood properties, since Verkier blood cured disease including the Black Death.
Dr. Simeon had removed Vicho's fangs for research, though they eventually grew back.

For two years, small vampire-spawn creatures (called 'wrongs' or corrupted cobalts) had been eating the imprisoned Isbrand alive piece by piece while his regenerating body continually absorbed their corruption.
The matriarch explained that Brenis had defeated Isbrand in battle, then forced the Uryashi to imprison him in chains within their caves under threat of destroying the village.
Lacra reveals that Brenus's weak point is his own sire, a powerful and older vampire.
A note found on a corpse revealed that an apprentice named Svetana, acting for her master Aurelius, hired mercenaries to retrieve an encoded tome from a tomb beneath St. Tobias's cemetery.
Cohen recalled that the dying Mihi in the crypt beneath Zvatra Cathedral had told him to trust the Augurs because they would save him.
Aurelius's records showed that in his most recent batch, only 3 of 11 prisoners successfully became gargoyles.
A previous squad sent by Leonard into Zanthy's castle never returned.
Brenis's coronation ritual is set to culminate in the sacrifice of every prisoner in his castle dungeons, including Cohen's family.
Brencis's story bridges two eras: Imperial Rome in 131 AD and the apocalyptic 14th century Carpathians, where the game's vampire plot takes place.
In Maragir, villagers celebrated Ambress's execution of former nobility by crucifixion, and feared Cohen as the Verkier-hunting dawn walker.
Cohen and Julen found Vera dead at an old pagan shrine after she went alone to find something to protect Julen from the poison.
After killing Ambress, Cohen found a report revealing that a new female Verkier had appeared near the northeastern wall of Svartra.
Ambrus's operations and reputation thrived as boyar until Coen began interfering with his draining dungeons.
When Coen disrupted his dungeons, Ambrus retaliated by sending a message through drained noble corpses and publicly hanging nobles, blaming the deaths on Coen.
Ambrus sent Coen a letter challenging him to an honorable duel to the death at the top of a hill by Marager, to be initiated by ringing an old bell at night.
Farcus's journal later revealed the ring's ritual to heal Ducen failed, crumbling to ash, after which Farcus went mad and mutilated his brother trying to fix him.
At the crime scene, Cohen found a threatening note from Dr. Simeon demanding D'vorah and Eli repay a debt by week's end.
It was actually the transformed Dr. Simeon, not Vicho, who killed D'vorah and Eli during his mutation.
Cohen later discovered that Vicho, having lost control of his hunger, slaughtered a farm family who had known his secret, after Simeon had falsely blamed Vicho beforehand.
Cohen found a manumit scout named Buen dying, who revealed the Verkieri were constructing an army of artificial winged creatures rather than recruiting soldiers.
Buen's dying message included the code word 'Teayotim,' which referred to the ruined Church of St. Teotim in the Midens.
In the negotiation route, after Cohen kills Brenis's three major vassals Ambress, Baker, and Zanthy and reaches maximum infamy, Brenis offers a parley at Shrikes Crag.

At the parley, Brenis brings Pater as proof that Cohen's family is alive and offers to return them and spare Lasa, including exemption from the blood tithe, in exchange for the location of the Manummit hideout.
Cohen can accept the bargain by marking the Manummit hideout entrance for Brenis, leading to its forces massacring the Manummits.
Brenis personally captures Craig during the raid on the Manummit hideout, drinking his blood and taking him away.
After consuming the Mandre and preparing fully, Cohen receives an invitation from Brenis proposing negotiations.
In the Lakra route, Cohen and Lakra descend into the ruins beneath Zvatra to interrupt Brenis's ritual.
Francis claims to have ruled or dominated others for hundreds of years before Coen's rebellion.
Inside the ritual chamber, a huge red sphere of blood churns while prisoners float around it.
Lakra destroys the blood sphere, breaking the active blood conduit through which Brenis was drawing strength from Anahora.
In the Manummit route, the rebels launch a surprise attack on an outpost while Catalin's army attacks from the other side to break the blockade of Veil Sangora.
Cohen personally turns the wheel to open the gates, breaking the blockade of Veil Sangora.
In this route, the Manummits and Catalin's forces have not yet begun their operation, leaving Cohen and Lakra to infiltrate the castle alone.
Craig reports that Brenis is performing a ritual using prisoners inside the castle, but Catalin dismisses this as superstition.
In this route, Cohen's family is found fused into Anahora's growth spreading through the castle, in a worse state than in the Manummit route.
Cohen, Craig, Catalin, and fighters storm the castle through a secret passage beneath the mountains, the same route Catalin used to escape two years earlier when the Verkieri seized power.
Cohen and Craig find the prison cells empty, with no sign of where the prisoners were taken.
Catalin sends a group of Manummits on a suicidal assault to seize the armory despite their being too few in number.
Brenis blames Lakra for causing reality and Anahora to collide, and offers to let Cohen take his family and leave without pursuit.
Cohen refuses Brenis's offer and attacks him alongside Lakra.
During the battle, Brenis seriously wounds Lakra, but she is healed by the power of the Mandre flower she and Cohen had consumed earlier.
Cohen and Craig find the desecrated corpse of Kenaz Scander sitting on the throne.
Brenis attacks Catalin in the throne room, and Craig sacrifices himself to protect Catalin, resulting in Craig's death.
Brenis badly wounds Catalin and then leaves, telling Cohen that his family is already waiting for him.
After defeating Zanthy's blood guard, Cohen kills the wounded Catalin himself, refusing to let him rule Veil Sangora.
Cohen finds his family seated at a table in the castle's dining hall, shrouded in crimson mist, with his youngest sister Luca missing.
Brenis reveals his plan to break every bone in Cohen's body, nail him to a wall, and force him to watch his family drained one by one.
Defeated, Brenis cuts open his palm to release a cloud of bloody mist that drags both himself and Cohen into Anahora.

Before vanishing into Anahora's wastelands (or being defeated), Brenis/Francis refuses to reveal what happened to Luca, having secretly ensured beforehand that he would have 'the last laugh' even after death.
After the confrontation with Francis, a funeral is held for someone young who died, and Coen's mother is not told the truth about it.
Unlike most ancient Vrakhiri, Ambrus was born a low-status human (a peasant and low-ranking mercenary soldier) who endured years of poverty and humiliation, coming to hate Knyaz Skender.
Ambrus was turned into a vampire relatively recently compared to his Vrakhiri peers.
Cohen and Lakra share deeply personal memories in the marsh to attract the wisps and be guided to Kalas's lair.
In the memory, Isbrand tells Lacra that 'the orcas' (an enforcing vampire faction) will hunt down those who break vampiric law.
Vladimir was connected to a rebel cell in Svatra, the capital of Veil Sangora, planning an uprising against Vrakieri rule.
The Sanjani found Hila in the forest and brought her to live in their burrow, using magic to keep her a child for 10 years.
Craig (Marat) told Cohen that the Manumits plan to help Catalin, son of the former ruler Scander, overthrow Kinaz Brenis by opening the mountain pass gates from within.
Hila appears to be a young girl but has actually been kept childlike for 10 years by the magic of the Sanjani, small fae-like beings who live in burrows.
By this point in the story, two of Brenis's Boyars, Ambress and Bakir, were already dead, leaving only the witch Zanthy.
Ambress kept a private herd of humans to feed on despite Brenis officially forbidding that practice among the Verkieri.
Cohen was voted into the Manumits, a group opposing Verkieri tyranny, with only Dro voting against him.
Nebero serves the Council of Orgas, a group of superior Dawnwalkers who disapprove of Francis's claim to power.
The Council of Orgas wants to make Coen an offer he is expected not to refuse, viewing him as a rare and valuable Dawnwalker.
Nebaru offers Cohen a purpose from the Council of Augers, saying eternity is unbearable without one.
The Uryashi are a humanoid mountain people with great physical strength who are derogatorily called goatfaces by humans.
The Sanjani have a peculiar fascination with collecting human teeth as gifts for their rulers, called Sarinas.
Xanthe implies that Lacra answers to unnamed superiors who have significant influence over events.
It is theorized that Brencis founded the vampiric clan that Ambrose is now part of, based on shared heraldic symbolism between their armors.
Unlike Brencis and Ambrose, the vampires Zanthe and Bakir do not wear the shared heraldic emblem, suggesting they may belong to different houses or have different motivations.
Kinyaz Scender Dragosti ruled through fear and cruelty beyond that of his predecessors.
Brencis's noble status shaped his identity around the pursuit of social respect, influence, and legacy.
Brencis's ambition to become consul suggests he was an intelligent, strategic thinker familiar with the politics of late Rome.
Cohen is wary of helping Catalin because Scander nearly had Cohen and Luca killed the night the Verkieri seized power.
Cohen's father trained him in hand-to-hand combat before revealing the plot against Brenus.
Brencis was once a Roman senator and nobleman who was on track to become consul before his transformation into a vampire.
Before becoming a vampire, Brencis's original Roman name is transcribed in sources as Kaiser Beranius Lorentius.
Brenis claimed he had watched Veil Sangora for years and had decided to change its fate.
Lacra, reliving the memory, finally understands and accepts that she cannot undo her past mistakes with Isbrand.
Cohen's mother Esme suffered a mental breakdown after her son Alen drowned, the plague struck, and the Vrakieri took power.
Anka was found washing hands covered in strange occult symbols, which she refused to explain to Cohen.
Esme was coaxed into drinking her medicine after Cohen sang her a childhood lullaby about a little angel.
Pieta revealed he has years of military service and tested Cohen's swordsmanship in a sparring match.
Cohen fought and beat the village bully Vassel after Vassel insulted him and his mother.
Vassel's father Atanis had been abusing his son since childhood, which Cohen discovered when Atanis demanded Cohen beat Vassel further.
An old woman named Gremla was distraught after the banner she wove for Brenis's blood mass was stolen.
The villager Premil stole Gremla's banner to protest it hanging in the church in place of the cross, and Cohen convinced him to return it to protect Gremla from punishment.
A villager named Gavl asked Cohen to find his missing brother Lazar in the marshes.
Father Floren preached in the church, portraying Brenis as a savior who protected the people from plague, war, and famine.
Before being turned, Ambrus had a lover named Rosalia who loved him deeply.
Silas had been a physician before turning to dark magic, reportedly learning to animate inanimate objects and drain life from living beings.
Silas studied and corrupted ancient teachings including the Cabala, combining sacred texts with unholy rituals.
Brenus told Cohen that resisting a sire's commanded blood-drinking made Cohen 'malformed' and a disappointing, deficient result of the vampiric gift.
Cohen survived being struck down by sunlight after his confrontation with Brenus, which Brenus had not expected.
Cohen met Vulk, a blind old mercenary and former comrade of his father Pieta, living in an isolated shack.
Cohen remembers craving blood painfully after being turned, but afterward appeared to look like a normal human again.
Ambrus eagerly accepted Brencis's offer and became a Vrakir, serving as the right hand (boyar) of the Knyaz.
Ambrus relished seeing the former nobility submit to him and enjoyed his new power as a Vrakir.
A woman named Katnika repeatedly wrote to Ambrus asking to be turned into a Vrakir, but Ambrus ignored her.
Ambrus desperately seeks to prove his worth to Knyaz Brencis, focusing his efforts on running his draining dungeons to earn Brencis's approval, feeling indebted to him for the gift of immortality.
Omnia believed the devil answered her prayers in exchange for blood, leading her to attempt a magical ritual sigil.
Beyond supplying blood to Brencis and the other boyars, Ambrus used his dungeons to exact revenge on the nobility of Vale Sanguinar who had wronged the common people.
Albertus was a monk who served as chronicler under Kinaz Brenis, tasked with praising the ruler's virtues and hiding his sins.
Cohen's recurring nightmare was built around the drowning death of his younger brother Alen, a tragedy Cohen blamed himself for.
Cohen and Anchor confronted Omnia as she attempted to complete a blood ritual, resulting in her death.
Cohen considered finishing Omnia's ritual himself despite the risk of death, but Anchor stopped him by taking the ritual notes.
Ambrus's brutal punishments of corrupt nobles earned him the trust and favor of the common townspeople of Vale Sanguinar.
Common townsfolk believed Ambrus would not harm ordinary people, only the rich and powerful, and defended him when others spoke against him.
Despite running draining dungeons for Brencis's blood supply, Ambrus refused to drink from that collected blood and instead kept his own personal 'blood cows' who willingly offered themselves to him.
Brencis adopted the name 'Brencis' after his transformation, which is Slavic in origin.
Ambrus forced Yulian Caudren to beg on his knees for the 'honor' of having his blood drunk, using it as a form of psychological revenge for Yulian's earlier submission.
Ambrus mainly imprisoned old nobles, rich merchants, and corrupt monks in his dungeons, which made him seem like a lesser evil to the common people.
After losing his research, Albertus reportedly went mad and now lives on the streets.
The Skull King claims to have a daughter named Harica who would be left 'doomed and alone' if he died.
Cohen initially refuses to invite the Skull King into his mind, and the Skull King is taken by the unknown force.
Vicho revealed that Simeon, desperate to avoid death, had once asked to be turned into a Verkier, but Vicho refused.
Lacra is a vampire of the Rakir bloodline who ambushed and tortured the soldier Nish for information.
Lacra says she has been trying to find a way to kill Brenus for a long time before meeting Cohen.
Nish reveals he was forced to serve Brenus as a soldier to protect his own village from suffering.
Cohen encounters a dying man who mistakes him for someone named Tobias and recognizes Cohen as a fellow Dawnwalker by his eyes.
Anka decided to complete the ritual herself to atone for stopping Leonuka, and Cohen reluctantly agreed to let her do it alone.
The Tournament Lord forces a loser named Moth to retrieve a swallowed coin from another man's body via self-mutilation.
Lacra served as Coen's first mentor, teaching him what he needed to know as a Dawnwalker.
Farcus, a nobleman turned into a vampire thrall, serves the Tournament Lord alongside his younger brother Dusko, who is described as 'damaged goods.'
After the Tournament Lord's death, Farcus thanks Cohen and asks for help finding his family's heirloom ring.
Anka admitted to Cohen that she has had feelings for him for a long time.
A guard named Baklan told Lacra how to find a vampire-controlled village in search of information about Isbrand.

During a gargoyle (monstrous creature) attack, Sara's (Sarah's) spine was broken, leaving her paralyzed and mortally wounded; Craig killed her himself with a dagger—citing that she 'knew too much' and that vampire guards/Kinaz Brenis's forces were coming—rather than let her be captured alive.
Craig told Cohen that if Cohen were ever in Sarah's position, he should be killed rather than allowed to be taken alive by Brenis's forces.
Craig and Cohen sought out a rabbi named Mevasa, a scholar of ancient books and traditions, to translate the manuscript from the gargoyle's mouth.
Mevasa told Craig and Cohen that a man named Silas could translate the manuscript, but Silas has been dead for roughly 100 years.
Mevasa mentioned that a woman recently came to him asking about Silas, claiming to be conducting research for her master.
Craig recognized the name Aurelius as a legendary evil sorcerer in Svartra folklore, said to be able to drive people mad with a glance and to live in a tower south of Augusti.
Craig revealed his real name to Cohen as Marat, as a sign of trust.
Cohen agreed to help the Manumits' plan because it could help him recover his family.
The village elder, called Shime, demands that Cohen and Lacra prove their strength in combat before revealing Isbrand's location.
Inside the nightmare, Cohen finally accepted that Alen's death was not his fault and promised to forgive himself and remember his brother.
Before dying, Saint Mihi promised Cohen that beings called 'the augers' would eventually find him and explain what a dawn walker truly is.
After defeating Aurelius, Cohen followed a trail of glowing flyer garic mushrooms to a burrow inhabited by a girl named Hila.
Hila asked Cohen to find her brother Tonis and offered that her invisible friends could deliver a letter to Cohen's sister Luca in exchange.
Cohen found Tonis, Hila's brother, now an adult living among charcoal burners, still visiting a wooden palace to light candles for his long-vanished sister.
The Tsarina of the Sanjani refused to let Tonis stay with Hila permanently, allowing him only one visit per month.
The Tsarina argued that human life for a girl in that era meant hard labor and repeated childbirth, justifying keeping Hila in the burrow.
Cohen convinced the Tsarina to release Hila for a ransom of human teeth rather than waiting years.
The Sanjani revealed that Cohen became a Dawn Walker instead of an ordinary Verkieri because his blood contained a small amount of silver, weakening the transformation.
After Cohen paid the ransom in human teeth, the Tsarina agreed to send a letter to Luca telling her Cohen would come for the family soon.
Father Floren, the priest who preaches at the blood masses, sent soldiers to an ancient shrine of St. Mihi, leading Cohen to investigate the cobalt caves.
A soldier named Leonard told Cohen that young women were disappearing throughout Baroness Zanthy's lands and that she was responsible.
Heraclea is revealed to be Baroness Zanthy's daughter, the reason Zanthy abducted and murdered young women in her territory.
Following reports of a mysterious female Verkieri near Svartra's northeastern wall, Cohen tracked her down and met Lacra, who was also seeking to kill Brenis.
Lacra revealed that Brenis's greatest weakness is Isbrand, the Verkieri who originally turned him.
Lacra held a captive Uryashi named Nish, whose clan elder knew how to find Isbrand.
Cohen convinced Nish to reveal the route to the Uryashi elder by promising to try to save his own family from Brenis, and swore not to harm Nish's people.
After getting the information they needed from Nish, Cohen convinced Lacra to spare his life rather than kill him.
At the Uryashi village, Cohen's calm, non-violent conduct under provocation earned the trust of the clan matriarch, who agreed to help.
The matriarch warned Lacra never to return to the Uryashi village, threatening to bury her under stones, while declaring Cohen a friend of the Uryashi.
Lacra and Cohen discovered they are both progeny of Brenis (Brenus), making Isbrand their shared 'grandfather' figure in the vampire hierarchy and Cohen her 'brother in blood.'
Cohen and Lacra extracted Isbrand and moved him to an old watch fort in the mountains, though his body was severely damaged and his mind broken beyond normal recovery.
Lacra refuses to explain to Cohen why her teeth were torn out or why she was exiled.
Isbrand repented his failure to kill Brenis earlier and asked Cohen to absorb his essence so his soul would not fall prey to the entity ruling Anahora.

To attract the wisps and find Kalas's battlefield, Cohen and Lacra shared deeply personal memories: Cohen's account of his family and his drowned brother Alen, and Lacra's account of being married off as a child in Egypt and enduring years of abuse.
Lacra says she needs time alone with Isbrand to find a way to restore him, implying a personal connection to his fate.
Lacra tells Cohen about another vampire named Vitio living in the Alton Market near the butcher shop in Svatra, who is unhappy with Brenus's rule.
Ambress, one of Brenis's boyers, challenged Cohen to a one-on-one duel at a ruined fortress near Maragir.
After the memory sequence, Cohen and Lacra find the present-day, severely weakened Isbrand awake and aware, and Lacra offers to end his suffering, but he refuses her invitation to join with him.
Julen Codrin, a noble who swore loyalty to Ambress on the night the Verkieri seized power, secretly wanted Ambress dead.
Ambress forced Julen to kneel and beg for the honor of having his blood drunk, humiliating him repeatedly.
Julen planned to have Cohen poison the person Ambress would drink from before their duel to weaken him.
Vera was a poison expert living alone in the marshes who was preparing a ritual to strengthen the poison meant for Ambress.
Julen revealed that he himself was meant to be the poisoned victim whose blood Ambress would drink before the duel, intending for both himself and Ambress to die.
Cohen chose to leave Ambress's soul trapped in Anahora rather than carry it back.
Cohen buried Julen Codrin's body beside a mountain monastery.
Anka revealed that the Font of Life not only strengthens but restores youth, and admitted she is twenty years older than Cohen.
Anka wanted to use the Font of Life to become young again and start over, free of the darkness she let into herself through occult dealings.
Ambrus valued honor and expected Coen, as a fellow Vrakir, to respect the terms of a fair duel.
Ambrus expresses admiration and respect for Coen in his letters, making the poisoning betrayal feel personal to him.
There was only enough power in the Font of Life for one person, so Anka let Cohen drink from it instead of herself.
Cohen and Anka became romantically involved that night after leaving the font.
In Anahora, Ambrus is shown as resentful that he only lived for two years after being turned, since to him living meant being powerful.
In Anahora, Ambrus becomes fearful and begs for mercy, appealing to Coen's humanity in his final desperate moments.
Farcus Derrescu, a servant of the boyer Bakir, secretly wanted his master dead and approached Cohen for help.
Farcus offered Cohen entry into the tournament as 'the moth' so Cohen could get close enough to Bakir to kill him.
If invited in, Ambrus acts like a supportive but melancholic companion to Coen, warning him of dangers and admiring his actions.
Ultimately Ambrus remains loyal to Brencis until the end because he feels he owes Brencis a debt for his immortal gift.
As the winning contestant, Cohen was allowed into Bakir's treasury, refused to remove his mask, and asked for the amethyst ring, which Bakir claimed not to have.
In Anahora, Bakir, a sadist and masochist, welcomed torment rather than begging to return, but Cohen carried his soul back to the physical world anyway to deny him that satisfaction.
Cohen gave Farcus the demonic ring despite warning him of its danger, out of sympathy for Ducen's suffering.
Vicho is a Verkier collector of curiosities and forbidden knowledge who opposes Brenis's regime but refuses to join Cohen's war openly.
Vicho refuses to drink human blood and instead whips himself before a Christian cross, praying to be freed from his curse or granted death.
Vicho suspected he himself might have killed D'vorah and Eli during a blackout, as his hunger has grown harder to control with age.
Realizing what he had done, Vicho chose to meet the sunrise and die rather than continue killing, and asked Cohen to stay with him until dawn.
Sara, the manumit woman who had once betrayed Cohen into a trap, returned to tell him the manumits would vote on his membership.
Craig, leader of the Manumits, tasked Cohen with finding four missing manumit scouts after suspecting betrayal by a member named Lios.
Craig told Cohen that if he were ever captured, Cohen should kill him too rather than let him be taken alive.
Lakra knew disrupting the ritual carried great risk but did so believing that letting Brenis finish would cause an even larger-scale catastrophe.
Catalin, son of the former Kenaz Scander, is revealed to be selfish, cruel, and arrogant like his father.
Cohen's sister Jana begs him to run when he finds her fused into the growth.
Catalin is pleased that Brenis killed his father, since it removed an obstacle to his own claim to the throne.
Francis calls Coen 'my son' during their final confrontation, implying a father-son relationship between them.
Francis demands that Coen submit and bow to him, but Coen refuses.
Francis warns Coen that defying him puts Coen's family at risk.
Brenis says sunlight has always been his greatest weakness but claims he no longer fears it, demonstrating by passing his hand through a sunbeam.
Near the end of their encounter, the protagonist is revealed to be a traitor working against Bakir.
Nebaru (Nebero), a Vraker and Dawnwalker like Cohen working as an Arbiter for the Council of Augers, arrives shortly after Francis's/Brenis's defeat.
Coen of Lazlia is a Dawnwalker, a being that drinks blood and grows more powerful at night.
Anka is also leaving Veil Sangora to search for a way to remove the evil power and heal the symbols carved into her skin.
Nebero explains that Luca's humanity cannot be restored, but she can survive and even thrive in moonlight as a transformed creature.
Bakir offers the protagonist a form of death or 'homecoming,' which the protagonist declines.
Bakir (the Tournament Lord) refers to tournament contestants as 'vermin' until they win, after which he calls them his 'friends,' claiming they were all once human servants ('Verlin') like them.
Contestants who survive but do not win are promised an invitation to Bakir's feast.
During the tournament, the protagonist spares a defeated opponent who begs for mercy so he can return to his son.
Bakir mocks the protagonist's act of mercy, saying there is always room on his table for fools who show kindness.
The protagonist becomes the last contestant standing in the tournament, winning the right to retrieve Bakir's coin.
Fergus is Bakir's subordinate, threatened with having his tongue cut out for breaking a promise of discretion to the protagonist.
After winning, the protagonist is made to surrender both weapon and mask to Bakir's court as a condition of becoming his 'friend'.

Bakir (the Tournament Lord) gives the protagonist/Cohen a drink revealed to be blood rather than wine, explaining it comes from a single carefully selected donor—a baby girl—calling it a rare delicacy rather than mixed 'vile swill'.
Bakir asks the protagonist how he would like to die, claiming the way a man wishes to die reveals his true nature.
Bakir states that even his own kind cannot escape death, and recalls that his father was the only meal that ever gave him indigestion.
Bakir claims to have experienced nearly every extreme of suffering and cruelty in his long life, including torturing others and being tortured himself.
Coen is the protagonist of The Blood of Dawnwalker, a being called a Dawnwalker or Penumbro who possesses both human and vampiric traits.
Coen is human during the day and transforms into a creature of blood at night.
Coen has a limited amount of time to save his family while confronting the ruling Vrakhiri Court.
Ambrus hides a deep inferiority complex behind his immaculate clothing, perfect hair, and noble posture.
Even as a mortal, Bakir possessed an unquenchable thirst for slaughter.
As a Vrakhir, Bakir despises hiding in secrecy and revels in bloodshed, demanding to be the center of attention.
Centuries of decay have affected Xanthe's body and mind, causing her to whisper to unseen spirits.
Although Xanthe appears insane to mortals, she understands the fundamental cosmic nature of the world better than anyone else in the Vrakhiri Court.
Anka once served as a novice at St. Tina's Convent, where forbidden magical books were kept.
Xanthe kidnaps young women and keeps them hidden inside her keep.
A terrified servant guards the Painted Door and begs visitors not to touch or open it, fearing that doing so will summon the mistress of the keep.
Xanthe's daughter is named Harriclaire and wears a mask.
Xanthe says Harriclaire is the one thing she lives for and the reason she continues to exist.
Xanthe killed multiple kidnapped women because she believed it was necessary to keep Harriclaire alive.
Xanthe claims that without her, Harriclaire would be lost or would die.
Xanthe states that Harriclaire's soul remains intact, which she calls practically a miracle.
Xanthe warns that nothing she creates or restores can last forever, at least not yet.
Xanthe hears mysterious voices that interrupt her and that she refuses to fully explain to Coen the Dawnwalker.
Xanthe reveals that Brennes was merely a convenience for her plans but has now become an obstacle.
Xanthe says Brennes seeks power he should not have and will not be able to control.
Xanthe states that Brennes endangered her daughter Harriclaire through his pursuit of forbidden power.
Xanthe claims that ruling over peasants alone was not enough for Brennes; he desires something greater that she refuses to name.
Xanthe offers to help Coen the Dawnwalker defeat Brennes in exchange for her own survival and that of Harriclaire.
Xanthe tells Coen the Dawnwalker that sparing her is more convenient for her plans, not an act of reason or mercy.
Brennes used Coen the Dawnwalker's family as leverage, removing them from the dungeon to ensure Coen's cooperation.
Brennes is aware that Coen the Dawnwalker is coming for him.
Lacra is present when Xanthe strikes her deal with Coen the Dawnwalker and comments on his resourcefulness.
Unlike Ambrus, the boyar Bekir is characterized as a rapist who enjoyed hurting people for pleasure.
Unlike Ambrus, the boyar Zanthi is characterized as someone who stole from and dismembered women.
Brencis's concept art depicts him with sickly, papery gray skin, sunken eyes, visible deformities, and ulcers on his scalp, appearing frozen in a state of decay.
Brencis's psychological profile is theorized to be built on three patterns: parasitic existence, manipulation, and a belief in his own superiority.

St. Tina's Convent became shrouded in a permanent unnatural fog after the plague struck the pilgrims who sought refuge there; it is near Veil Sangora and avoided by locals, who hear the nuns singing at night as the fog spreads.
Hila's home village of Augusti was abandoned years ago after its inhabitants died of plague or left.
Kalas had the power to thin the veil between reality and Anahora.
Lacra and Cohen agree to meet at a landmark called Crown Rock Knight to continue their search for Isbrand.
Craig and Cohen discovered Silas's former home, which had a hidden cellar leading to ancient ruins where Silas conducted his experiments.
The ancient ruins beneath Silas's house connect to catacombs from the Christian era, where Cohen and Craig found fresh decapitated bodies.
Cohen and Lacra travel to a village ruled by Rakiri soldiers to find the location of Isbrand.
Saint Mihi called Cohen a 'dawn walker' and claimed to be one himself.
The village elder reveals Isbrand is trapped in a cave at the village's end, blocked by rock, where he is kept fed but never freed.
Inside Zanthy's castle, Cohen found a laboratory where the Baroness performed horrific mutilations on abducted girls, removing bones and eyes.
A dungeon beneath Zanthy's castle contained piles of human remains fed to a monster kept in the cellar.
Cohen and Anka searched for the Font of Life using clues from an old monk's diary, discovering ancient ruins in the mountains.

The Discord bot message states that before Brencis's arrival, people suffered plague, war, famine, and death, and that Brencis came to heal and protect them, in exchange for blood as a price for safety.

A Latin verse associated with Brencis, translated into English, describes his followers offering to return his gifts of strength, hope, and medicine by letting him drink their blood as he drinks from them.
Despite clearing the Rockfalls range of Cobalts, their caves remain dangerous, as other threats are hidden there.
Veil Sangora is a principality located deep in the Carpathian Mountains.
The wisps lead Cohen and Lakra to an overgrown entrance to Kalas's lair.
Xanthe's home is boarded up completely, allowing no sunlight to enter.
Cohen found only his father's old equipment and a prayer book from Marrair Monastery in a hidden cache instead of gold.
The cobalts divided Mihi's shattered sword among three nests, treating each fragment as a sacred relic.
Vulk left Cohen his sword and a note saying he was leaving for one last adventure rather than remain a burden.
Bakir promised Farcus the demonic ring could work miracles and might heal Ducen if Farcus impressed him.
The dying man possesses a broken sword and tells Cohen to seek smiths to reforge it, warning that something unseen is watching and growing inside Cohen.
The tome sought by Svetana's mercenaries was written in the same unknown language as the manuscript from the gargoyle's mouth and Silas's writings.
Cohen seeks a ring heirloom belonging to the Dresco family, which the Tournament Lord claims is not in his treasury.
Cohen and Anka found a book titled Sancti Mihi Histori Vera whose pages appeared blank, written in invisible ink.
Cohen found a parchment drawing in Silas's ruins depicting a gargoyle nearly identical to the ones encountered at the warehouse and St. Teotim's church.
Inside the tower, Cohen found a translation guide and a spellbook that let him decipher the strange language and use magic, including a spell to weaken gargoyles.
Leonard gave Cohen a magic lamp that, when placed in the hand of a statue by Zanthy's gate, would remove the impenetrable barrier protecting her castle.
Lacra hoped that Kalas's old lair might contain something to protect them from Anahora's influence or to turn Brenis's ritual against him.
Anka found a manuscript describing the Impluvium vite, or Font of Life, said to grant anyone who enters it strength greater than Achilles.
Farcus is the true heir to the title of Bandrescu and wanted an amethyst family ring from Bakir's treasury to prove his lineage.
The amethyst ring recovered was engraved with demonic runes from Anahora rather than the Drescu family crest.
Vicho offered Cohen a protective amulet in exchange for help investigating the deaths of his friends D'vorah and Eli.
A manuscript written in an unknown language and marked with an unfamiliar occult symbol was found rolled up inside a gargoyle's mouth; Craig planned to have a rabbi named Measer translate it.
Anka prepares a lethal potion for Cohen, warning it is dangerous, intending it to be used that same night.
The potion Anka prepared is lethal poison to both Verkieri and Moroni, and Cohen intends to use it to end Luca's suffering.
Bakir tells contestants that the token is a precious coin hidden under a willow tree.
Bakir reveals that the coin had been swallowed by one of the defeated contestants, and demands the protagonist cut it out of the body.
Bakir shows the protagonist his treasury filled with gold, emeralds, fine weaponry, and ancient relics.
The banner used in Brenis's blood mass depicted a hellish scene with a tree impaling bodies, a lake of blood, feasting Vrakieri, and a three-eyed fanged god-like entity.
Growing within Kalas's remains is a Mandre, an extremely rare flower of Anahora.
The Mandre is said to grant power that can help someone withstand both Brenis and Anahora itself.
Cohen and Lakra both consume the Mandre flower.
Xanthe used resin in rituals performed on the bodies of the kidnapped women.
Ambrus's chest armor bears a symbol similar to Brencis's armor, reflecting his lifelong pattern of serving others.
Brencis's armor is archaic and ceremonial but functional, featuring spikes and a grim, medieval-inspired stylization rather than authentic Roman design.
Brencis's armor includes a belt and robe with patterns reminiscent of Roman mosaics, suggesting an effort to preserve his Roman legacy visually.
Brencis's armor resembles Ambrose's armor in style, including chain mail and a chest plate, suggesting Brencis adapted to a more medieval aesthetic despite his Roman origins.
Brencis's original concept art color scheme uses rich bronze and black tones to evoke nobility.
Brencis's armor features a stylized double-headed dragon emblem across his chest, theorized to be a distorted version of the Roman legionary standard, the aquila.
A jagged, tooth-like pattern appears at the center of the dragon emblem on both Brencis's and Ambrose's armor, possibly symbolizing vampire teeth, lineage, or house allegiance.
Ambrose's version of the shared emblem is sleeker and more refined than Brencis's, suggesting the symbol and legacy evolved over time.
Brencis's armor includes spiked pauldrons, chain mail, and a detailed ceremonial blade at his hip, reinforcing his role as a commander and strategist rather than a mere nobleman.
Saint Mihi's sword was shattered and its pieces were carried off by cobalts; Cohen would need to recover the fragments and have Yurashi blacksmiths reforge it.
Cohen killed Brenis's soldiers who had raided the third cobalt cave and recovered the final sword fragment.
A Yurashi blacksmith agreed to reforge Mihi's sword for free once she learned Cohen intended to kill Brenis.
Cohen empowered the reforged sword with nameless magical power inside an ancient ruin in the mountains, making it deadly against both humans and monsters.
Cohen defeated an undead guardian protecting the ancient warrior's tomb in the cave.
Coen's first encounter with Brencis occurs in a narrative showcase fight at Laslea Glen during the prologue.
A mysterious figure called the Skull King confronted Cohen, dismissing him as a 'half-breed' failed creation of Brenus.
Cohen ultimately fights and kills the Tournament Lord after he reveals he recognizes Cohen as the one sabotaging his operation.
Cohen found Saint Mihi walled in alive beneath the cathedral in Svartra, emaciated but still breathing after centuries of imprisonment.
Saint Mihi mistook Cohen for a man named Tobias and attacked him with a broken sword.
Cohen infiltrated Aurelius's tower to stop him from creating more gargoyles for Brenis, killing Svetana and a garrison of Brenis's soldiers.
At the top of his tower, Aurelius was seen performing an incantation before a gargoyle, surrounded by images of Anahora, suggesting he draws power from Anahora to animate and control gargoyles.
Cohen escaped the nightmare and woke to find Aurelius preparing to turn him into a gargoyle on a table; Cohen killed Aurelius with a hammer blow.
In an upper chamber of the castle, Cohen found a masked, mutilated creature named Heraclea, stitched together from the bodies of abducted girls, singing a mournful song.
Baroness Zanthy offered to help Cohen fight Brenis in exchange for sparing her and Heraclea, but Cohen refused and killed both the Baroness and Heraclea.
After the vision, Isbrand's remaining spirit attacked Cohen and Lacra but was defeated with little difficulty.
Cohen and Lacra kill the feral wrongs that were devouring Isbrand's body, ending their self-destructive feeding cycle.
The present Isbrand reveals a mysterious sphere artifact and demands Cohen submit to him in exchange for possibly helping find Cohen's family.
Cohen refuses to bow to Isbrand, leading to a final confrontation between them.
At the duel, Ambress drank Julen's poisoned blood after Cohen refused to drink first and insulted Ambress's manners.
Weakened by the poison, Ambress was defeated by Cohen, who then drank his blood.
Cohen fought and killed Bakir in the treasury after being denied the ring, then drank his blood and was pulled into Anahora.
Dr. Simeon's failed self-transformation turned him into a Muron, and Cohen and Vicho were forced to kill him.
At the Church of St. Teotim, Cohen and Sara were ambushed by a gigantic winged creature made from a mutilated human body sealed inside a clay vessel.
Despite Brenis no longer fearing sunlight, Cohen, who arrived in human form during the day, fights and defeats him in the physical world.
In Anahora, Brenis transforms into a deformed monster with a flayed skull and leathery tentacles.
Cohen defeats Brenis's monstrous form within Anahora itself, something normally considered impossible.
Coen ultimately defeats Francis in single combat without Lacra's assistance.
Bakir chooses to remain and be destroyed with his victims rather than accept the offered release, claiming he has experienced every horror except this one.
The final battle against Brencis is a two-phase climax fight that takes place at Griefberg Castle and Anachora.
Brencis is the Knyaz of Vale Sangora, also known as the Grotesque Ascendant.
Ambrus holds the title of the Right Fist of the Knyaz, serving Brencis.
Ambrus is fought in the Maragir Wealds region.
Ambrus is a highly aggressive swordmaster who uses fast dash strikes and blood-infused parries.
Bakir is known as the Mad Khan among the Vrakhiri Court.
Bakir is fought at Lunar Manor.
Bakir is a relentless brute-force fighter combining heavy weapon sweeps with erratic blood-magic charges.
Xanthe is called the Dark Mistress and is the oldest active member of the Vrakhiri Court.
Xanthe is fought at Svartrau Cathedral.
Xanthe's boss fight is widely considered the most punishing in the game, using blood-orb siphon mechanics, mirror illusions, and summoned Knight Bannerets to defend her altar.
Inside the lair, Kalas is found fused into a mass of plant-like growth resembling the vegetation seen in Anahora and in Baroness Zanthy's castle.
Cohen encountered and killed a brood of cave-dwelling creatures called cobalts after being turned.
Anka and Cohen found the convent's novices resurrected as undead, singing prayers and attacking intruders.
The gargoyle creatures are built around a clay vessel containing a human body with amputated limbs, baked as if in an oven.
While exploring the crypt, Craig was attacked and dragged off by a moroni creature living in the tomb, but Cohen saved him.
Zanthy's castle was guarded by leathery blood-cord creatures and monstrous dog-like beasts created from feeding dogs human remains.
The caves holding Isbrand were infested with cobalts whose cave art depicted an upside-down Verkieri (Isbrand) being worshipped.
Cohen and Lacra encountered corrupted, mutated cobalts that had broken from the cobalt hive mind due to exposure to the same corruption that creates Verkieri.
The cobalt hive mind, called the Hive, referred to the mutated, hive-severed cobalts as 'wrongs,' the strongest of which was named Chonk.
Cohen and Anka defeated mummified undead guardians who had failed the font's trials before them.
Cohen defeated the gargoyle creature, discovering it was constructed from an amputated human body baked inside clay, with wings and bony scythe-like limbs attached.
Brenis's last remaining gargoyle and soldiers guard the underground ruins, and the intrusion awakens the undead.
Coen, together with Lacra, kills every Cobalt (a kobold-like creature) in the Rockfalls mountain range.
Pieter is an aged mercenary veteran defending his village who has been driven mad by vampire blood contamination.
Pieter is found in the Laslea Glen and Boar's Back region.
The Ravenous Bear is a massive woodland predator mutated by drinking run-off Vrakhiri blood from nearby mass graves.
The Forgotten Guardian is an ancient stone automaton left behind by a forgotten classical civilization.
The Vrakhiri Banneret is a patrolling commander who enforces Brencis's blood tax.
The Chief Jailor is a sadist appointed to manage human captives destined for blood harvests, found in the Briar Sloughs region.
Cerbus the Scornful is a rogue Vrakhir knight who was banished to the swamps of Briar Sloughs.
Rayko the Incorruptible is a former Holy Order paladin who succumbed to vampirism but still recites hymns during combat.
The Murohn Malformed Monstrosity is a terrifyingly distorted failed vampire mutation that lurks in deep bog caverns in Briar Sloughs.
The Pack Leader is a dire shadow-wolf alpha infused with vampiric essence, found in Briar Sloughs.
The Renegade Bruiser is an outlaw champion who rules over swamp bandits in Briar Sloughs.
The Great Bog Wurm is a colossal subterranean serpent lurking beneath the marshes of the Maragir Wealds and Rockfalls region.
The Bloodletter is a Vrakhiri executioner specializing in blood magic rituals, found in the Maragir Wealds and Rockfalls region.
Munch-Munch is a towering, ravenous ogre-like creature infesting mountain caves in the Maragir Wealds and Rockfalls region.
The Essence of Grief is a spectral manifestation of plague victims' agony, found in the Maragir Wealds and Rockfalls region.
The Almshouse Monstrosity is a massive Murohn formed from infected plague victims trapped inside a quarantined asylum in Svartrau City.
Mihai is a legendary ancient knight resurrected as an undead guardian in Svartrau City.
Rurg the Honourable is a duelist who challenges Coen to test his strength, found in Svartrau City.
Ursul the Undefeated is a former gladiatorial champion turned night hunter, found in Svartrau City.
Wisps are otherworldly entities that inhabit the marshes and are drawn to and guided by strong, sincere emotions such as joy, grief, or anger.
The servant at the keep feeds pieces of the kidnapped women to a dog kept somewhere in the boarded-up yard.
In the turncoat ending, Brenis honors the bargain and returns Cohen's family, and the story moves to Lasa instead of a final battle.
In the turncoat ending, Cohen never confronts Brenis in Anahora and never kills him.
In the turncoat ending, Brenis remains in power and continues extracting blood from the valley for his larger plan, while Lasa receives special privileges including permission for Christianity.
In the epilogue, Cohen learns at a cemetery that Luca has died, but the rest of his family survived.
Cohen visits his mother Esme, who is catatonic, but she briefly regains awareness long enough to tell him she loves him.
Cohen helps his father Pieta repair the front door of their home, though conversation between them remains difficult.
Cohen announces he is leaving Veil Sangora, and Pieta gives him his blessing.
Cohen finds Luca alive in a mountain cave, transformed into a Muron rather than dead as everyone believed.
Brenis's farewell gift to Cohen was transforming Luca into a Muron instead of killing her.
Nebaru (also called Nebero) gives Cohen a letter with instructions and says they must leave the valley immediately before snow buries the mountain passes.
Nebaru (also called Nebero) stays behind to deal with the chaos left by Brenis/Francis and his remaining servants and followers, promising that in time no one will remember Brenis's name.
In the Lakra ending route, when Nebaru comes to the cave, Lakra arrives with him and reveals she works for the Council of Augers, who sent her to deal with Brenis.
After Francis's defeat, Lacra leaves Veil Sangora, frustrated that Coen finished the fight without her help.
Coen agrees to answer the Council of Orgas's call after Nebero's offer.
Nebero mentions that Coen's sister 'cannot wait', implying another sibling is in danger elsewhere, setting up future events.
That same night, Cohen loads Luca into a wagon and leaves the valley.
In every ending route, Luca is transformed into a Muron and Nebaru eventually comes for Cohen, who enters the service of the Council of Augers.
Coen prevents Anchor from finishing a ritual that was originally started by a character named Leona, due to unknown risks.
Coen's mother shows some improvement in health for a few days after the main events, and Coen treasures this time with her.
The epilogue of the turncoat ending states that Brenis's regime eventually collapses because of the arbiters, meaning Cohen's choice only delays rather than secures Brenis's rule.
Years later, people tell stories of a lone hero who stormed Francis's castle and slew him, and these stories become half-believed legends.
After Francis's death, no one pays to maintain the city guard of Svatra, so it disbands.
With the city guard gone, gangs of ruffians roam the streets of Svatra, and violence becomes common.
Without the ritual use of 'viceri blood', the plague returns to Veil Sangora after Francis's fall.
The Ourashi retreat permanently to villages high in the mountains after the events in Veil Sangora.
Religious images and references to the god Rkeri are removed and forbidden following the events in Veil Sangora.
Anchor's relationship with Coen's father ends because the local priest disapproved of women like her.
Monsters retreat into hiding after Francis's defeat but do not disappear entirely from Veil Sangora.
After Francis's fall, shepherds occasionally experience rockslides, a sign that the Ourashi still exist nearby.
The villagers of Veil Sangora eventually accept Luca despite her transformation into a beast.
Coen and Morat become close friends after the main conflict, despite disagreeing about the valley's future.
Local fighters who hoped to retire peacefully after the monsters were gone instead find themselves dying in conflicts with other humans.
Coen's fate becomes permanently intertwined with his sister Luca's after her transformation.
Lacra travels to distant lands after leaving Veil Sangora, continuously evading pursuers and causing destruction.
Brenis instituted a weekly Blood Mass where the Vrakieri drink blood from every resident of Veil Sangora in every local church.
During the blood mass, villagers drank a sip of Brenis's blood from a communion chalice and then gave their own blood into a baptismal font.
After the fall, Cohen's broken bones healed instantly and he discovered he could dissolve into black mist to cross gaps.
Newly turned, Cohen discovered he could climb walls and ceilings, ignoring gravity.
Cohen discovered he does not burn in sunlight, unlike ordinary Vrakieri, making him an unprecedented and dangerous anomaly.
Anka used a ritual involving runes carved into Cohen's flesh to unlock hidden magical perception, allowing him to see beyond ordinary reality.
Anchor explains that the standard vampiric transformation, called the Vra Fang, did not fully take hold on Cohen.
Cohen rang the convent's bells to trigger the undead nuns' ingrained routine of gathering for prayer, clearing a path to the library.
In Ambrus's draining dungeons, prisoners were hung upside down and drained of blood using leeches until death.
Any of Ambrus's subordinates who failed to maintain the dungeons properly were punished on the racks.
The Skull King offers Cohen the choice to either let his soul be consumed by the entity or to invite the Skull King's essence into Cohen's own mind.
Winners of the Luna Tournament are promised rewards including food, riches, and an invitation to the Tournament Lord's feast, while losers remain 'famine.'

Aurelius's gargoyle creation process involved keeping captives' higher brain functions active in a mental trap, then gutting them, coating them in clay, firing them, and fitting them with limbs, wings, and blades before animating them in a ritual.
The moment Cohen entered Aurelius's hall, he was trapped in a magical nightmare snare shaped from his own memories.
The Hive offered to reveal Isbrand's location if Cohen and Lacra killed the wrongs, including Chonk.
To retrieve useful information from Isbrand's shattered mind, Cohen and Lacra had to enter Anahora and follow the remnants of his memories.
Cohen drove Isbrand's fang into his own heart, absorbing the ancient Verkieri's essence and saving his soul from Anahora.
Cohen and Lacra theorized that the ruins beneath Svatra might connect directly to the castle's underground levels, allowing them to disrupt the ritual and free the prisoners in one operation.
Cohen and Lacra enter a shared vision or memory-space to relive Isbrand's past using some form of blood-memory magic.
Using Vera's notes, Cohen completed the poison ritual and forced Julen to drink the mixture, binding the poison to his blood.
In Anahora, Ambress's spirit begged Cohen to carry his soul back into the living world, since living Verkieri can host echoes of other Verkieri's essence.
To enter the Font of Life, Cohen had to pass warrior's trials without armor, marked with magical symbols painted by Anka.
The trials included revenants, deadly traps, and a statue that flayed Cohen's arm to test his willingness to sacrifice.
If the player chooses, Coen can use Yulian Caudren to poison Ambrus instead of facing him in a fair duel, which shocks and disappoints Ambrus.
After drinking from the font, Cohen felt all his exhaustion and pain vanish, gaining renewed strength.
When Coen defeats Ambrus, the player can choose to kill him outright or drain his blood and later meet his spirit in Anahora.

Bakir (also called the Tournament Lord) hosts a recurring contest known as the Luna Tournament (or 'rat race'), held inside a maze — variously described as beneath a willow tree, in a ruined fortress, or at the heart of a labyrinth.
Coen can choose to leave Ambrus to fade into a Leech Ghost and return to his maker, or invite him into an alliance.
The same choice to kill or invite Ambrus occurs even if Coen heads straight for the castle instead of dueling him at the hill.
Cohen won the lunar tournament by retrieving a coin that had been swallowed by another contestant, the porcupine, cutting it from his belly.
Simeon experimented on living subjects, including himself, attempting to turn humans into Verkieri by driving a fang into the heart.
Cohen faces a choice: negotiate with Brenis, join Catalin and the Manummits to break the blockade at the mountain pass, or join Lakra to sabotage Brenis's ritual beneath Zvatra.
Nebero explains that an Arbiter is someone who resolves crises like the one that occurred in Veil Sangora.
Nebaru explains there is a way to transform a Muron into a true Vrair, meaning Luca cannot become human again but need not remain a mindless monster.
Contestants in the Luna Tournament hide their identities by wearing masks shaped like vermin or other animals, such as moths or porcupines.
The goal of the Luna Tournament is to reach the heart of the maze, retrieve a hidden token or coin, and present it to a boy (or the Tournament Lord).
Bakir declares that in the tournament biting, kicking, and cheating are all permitted and nothing is forbidden or dishonorable.
Bakir warns that if no contestant retrieves the coin by dawn, all contestants will remain 'vermin'.
Ambrus can be weakened before his duel if the player completes the side quest 'The Bittersweet Toast'.
Cohen transforms into a Vrakieri at night but remains human by day, an unexplained unique condition.
Cohen must defeat Brenis's three boyers, Ambress, Bakir, and Zanthy, before confronting Brenis himself.
Among Verkieri, forcibly removing another vampire's teeth is a ritualized punishment and humiliation.
To enter Xanthe's keep, Coen the Dawnwalker must use a special lantern on a statue beside a strange door.
Brencis's intended tone in narration is authoritative, ancient, calm yet terrifyingly detached.
Extracted voice lines for Ambrus total less than 30 minutes of dialogue.
A typical playthrough of the Ambrus storyline takes less than 10 minutes, which is seen as a missed opportunity for a deeper alliance questline.

The name 'Brencis' is theorized to derive from the Slavic word 'breza' (meaning 'birch tree'), which the game's creators may have mistakenly interpreted as meaning 'laurel' or 'bay leaf,' intending it to symbolically mean 'one crowned with laurel' reflecting his status as a man of great accomplishment.
A message from the official Dawnwalker Discord bot refers to Brencis as 'your shepherd,' framing him as a caretaker figure to his followers.
In early concept art Brencis was depicted with hair, but in his final in-game appearance he is bald with a smooth scalp.
A fan-made 'redhead Brencis' image exists as a meme created by a Discord server member named Lord Dracula.
A second, grayscale version of Brencis's concept art strips away color, possibly representing an alternate design option considered by the developers.
The analyst has previously created character analyses for Ambrose, Bakir, and Zanthe, and expresses anticipation for future lore on a character named Cohen.
A post-credits scene reveals Cohen survives into the modern day, still fighting supernatural forces as Anahora's corruption begins seeping into the real world again.
Only four people knew of the convent's forbidden library: Anka, Leonica, Mother Superior Bernice, and caretaker Anel.
Among the recovered forbidden books was one titled Sancti Mihi Histori Vera, written in invisible ink, revealing that Saint Mihi actually fought the Vrakieri rather than dragons as commonly believed.
Ambrus saw himself as having rid his people of evil and believed he was fundamentally different from the corrupt nobility he destroyed.
After being defeated, the Skull King describes an entity that wants to meld with his soul and strip away his personhood.
The Tournament Lord claims he replaced an 'evil' predecessor called Lord Scander, but Cohen argues he merely replaced one tyrant with another.
Brenis was attempting to create a controlled breach into Anahora to draw power into the material world while retaining control, but Lakra's sabotage left the breach uncontrolled.
By the end of his journey, Coen fully embraces his vampiric nature instead of fearing it.
Bakir claims that the treasure itself has no true value to him, and that what he truly values is power over others.

Cohen suspects Anahora is the world depicted on the blasphemous banner in Lazla's church, showing a three-eyed fanged figure devouring Verkieri and their victims, and theorizes it may be the same being Leonuka bargained with.
The narrator theorizes that the gargoyles' construction, human bodies sealed in fired clay, is inspired by the concept of golems from Jewish folklore.
Isbrand believed Verkieri should remain hidden and obey ancient restrictions, while Brenis wanted to abandon restraint and openly dominate humanity.
Lakra believes Kalas was meddling with the same power that Brenis is trying to harness.
Lakra suspects Kalas's unusually deep connection to Anahora is what preserved his body in plant form.
Brenis later explains his goal was to embrace and harness the Anacorin curse carried by the Verkieri rather than resist it.
Xanthe implies that everyone eventually hears these voices and that no one has ever escaped them.
Xanthe tells Coen the Dawnwalker that his heart remains regrettably human, suggesting he struggles with his transformation.
Ambrus's dialogue suggests he might have been willing to turn against Brencis and form an alliance with Coen instead.
Among the three boyars, Ambrus is considered the most redeemable, since he mainly targeted corrupt nobles rather than innocents.
Brencis is theorized to bring Roman ideals into the vampire world, including order through dominance, legacy through blood, and control through heraldry and hierarchy.
Brencis is interpreted as having built a cult rather than a traditional empire, using fear and ritual to maintain control over his followers.

The double-headed dragon emblem on Brencis's armor is theorized to represent duality: the mortal and immortal aspects of his existence, his Roman origin versus his vampire future, or his inner conflict between discipline and monstrous hunger.
It is theorized that Brencis sees vampirism not merely as survival but as a new form of civilization, a twisted continuation of Roman order.
It is theorized that Brencis's unfulfilled human ambition to become consul resurfaces in his vampiric goal of founding 'House Brencis' as a new form of empire.
It is theorized that Brencis did not seek world domination over all mortals, which may explain why vampires in the game invaded only a small region rather than the whole world.
It is theorized that Brencis recruits followers through ideology and vision rather than brute force, offering them a place in his new vampiric order.
It is theorized that Brencis presents himself as a messianic figure who brings order to a plague-ridden, chaotic Europe.
Brencis's story is interpreted as a founding myth for vampire society, one that other vampires may revere, fear, or rebel against.
The analyst describes Brencis as both a cautionary tale and a power fantasy, a man who lost everything and rebuilt it amid the chaos of a plagued world.
