In The Blood of Dawnwalker, Brencis is framed not simply as a villain but as a founder-type character, akin to a ruler or father figure representing the caregiver archetype.

events.summary: In ancient Rome (131 AD), a wealthy noble named Caeso Burrienus Laurentius (later Brencis) is born into a life of privilege, aiming to become consul.
Brencis's army is destroyed in battle; he and survivors flee into a shadow-haunted place where the ancient vampire Isbrand offers him the choice to kneel and become Verkieri or die, and he submits.
Newly turned, Brencis is forced by Isbrand to kill the guards of his own estate and confront his wife, who fails to recognize him and burns herself alive, severing his human ties.

Over the following centuries other ancient figures are drawn into the Verkieri world: Xanthe (a Greek priestess), Bakir (a Hun warrior captured, tortured, and later turned and tormented by Arachia before killing him), and Isbrand punishes his progeny Lacra for violating vampire law, tearing out her teeth and exiling her.

In a separate ancient era, the legendary Saint Mihi fought the Verkieri, including the ancient vampire Kalas, using a magically strengthened sword, but was betrayed by the monk Tobias and sealed alive underground, his legend twisted into a dragon-slaying myth and his sword shattered among cobalt nests.
A warrior woman who resisted the Verkieri long ago chose to burn herself rather than be turned, leaving behind a tomb later found by Cohen.

Isbrand and Brenis later clash beneath Svatra; Isbrand warns Brenis that the Augurs will punish him for breaking Verkieri law, but Brenis's three boyars (Bakir, Ambress, Zanthy) help him defeat and imprison Isbrand, who is left chained in Uryashi caves and slowly devoured for years by corrupted cobalts.
Kinyaz Scender Dragosti rules Veil Sangora with cruelty after taking the throne in 1324; nine years of oppression culminate in a peasant uprising that he brutally crushes at Shrikes Crag.
By 1347 the Black Death ravages Europe; amid the chaos, hidden Vrakhiri vampires emerge to seize control of human settlements, including Veil Sangora.

Fleeing soldiers with his dying sister Luca, Cohen is saved when Brenis and his three boyars ambush and slaughter Scender's soldiers; Brenis heals Luca with his blood, then drains and kills Scender himself, seizing Veil Sangora that night with Ambress, Bakir, and Zanthy.

Brenis abolishes taxes in exchange for a blood tithe, bans silver, seals the valley, forbids soldiers from killing humans, and institutes weekly Blood Masses where his cursed blood cures plague in exchange for the peasants' blood.

Separately, a low-born peasant named Ambrus, imprisoned and dying after defying Skender, is found by Brencis and Skender's other victims during Brencis's invasion of Vale Sanguinar; offered death or transformation, Ambrus chooses to become a Vrakir and helps slaughter the nobility, abandoning his lover Rosalia after a failed attempt to turn her leaves her a Moroi.
As Ambrus settles into power, he builds draining dungeons but channels his cruelty into punishing corrupt nobles rather than commoners, earning twisted public trust while hiding deep insecurity.

Meanwhile at St. Tina's Convent, Anka is expelled after her friend Leonica betrays her over forbidden magic; as plague ravages the convent, Leonica bargains with a dark entity, cursing the dying nuns to rot alive as undead.
Two years after the takeover (1349), the mining village of Lazla still pays the blood tithe; Cohen's mother Esme grows too weak for the Blood Mass, and his father Pieta sends him to Anka for a tonic.

Pieta and neighbor Vladimir, part of a Svatra resistance cell, plot to raid an abandoned silver mine for silver to use against the Vrakieri; Brenis publicly condemns Esme to death at the Blood Mass, provoking Cohen's outburst and forcing Pieta's hand.

Brenis's forces, forewarned, crush the rebellion at the silver mine; in the chaos Cohen is bitten by strange mist and moths, loses control and feeds on a wounded miner, and is turned into a Vrakieri by Brenis himself before being struck down into a mineshaft.

Brenis destroys Lazla in retaliation, takes Cohen's family captive, tortures Pieta to test Cohen's bloodlust, and ultimately defeats and impales Cohen, leaving him to die at dawn—unaware that Cohen's tainted blood actually weakens him.

Miraculously surviving sunlight, Cohen is found and healed by Anka, who discovers through necromancy that the captured villagers, including his family, are held for Brenis's coronation ritual in 30 days.

Cohen begins guerrilla resistance, meeting the blind mercenary Vulk (his father's old comrade), raiding Vrakieri camps, and uncovering fragments of his father's and Vulk's mercenary past, including Pieta's atonement for burning Cassell.
Cohen infiltrates Stonewood Post to free the miller Mert, is lured into a Manummit ambush by Sarah, and gradually earns the rebel leader Craig's trust, eventually being voted into the Manummits.

Investigating St. Tina's Convent's curse, Cohen and Anka kill Leonica mid-ritual, only to later learn she had been trying to free the cursed souls; Anka returns alone to complete the ritual herself, releasing the trapped nuns.

Elsewhere, Cohen uncovers the fate of a lost girl, Hila, kept ageless for a decade by the fae-like Sanjani, and negotiates with their Tsarina for her release and a message to Luca, while also learning his own blood carries a trace of silver—explaining his unique nature as a Dawnwalker rather than ordinary Verkieri.

Cohen roots out the sorcerer Aurelius and his apprentice Svetana, who have been constructing monstrous gargoyle-soldiers from mutilated captives using power drawn from Anahora and ancient texts once studied by the corrupted physician Silas; Cohen kills Svetana, escapes a memory-nightmare, and destroys Aurelius.
Cohen frees the imprisoned Saint Mihi, who names him a fellow 'Dawnwalker' and promises that beings called the Augurs will one day explain his nature before dying.

Cohen storms Baroness Zanthy's castle, uncovering her horrific experiments to keep her daughter Heraclea's soul intact by abducting and mutilating young women; he refuses her offer of alliance and kills both her and Heraclea.

Following reports of a new female Verkier, Cohen meets Lacra, who also seeks to kill Brenis; together, using the captive Uryashi Nish and the trust of the clan matriarch, they locate and extract the broken, half-devoured Isbrand from his prison.

Delving into Isbrand's shattered memories within Anahora (sharing their own traumatic pasts to navigate the vision), Cohen and Lacra relive his history and the truth of Brenis's origin; afterward, Isbrand repents and asks Cohen to absorb his essence rather than let his soul fall to Anahora, and the feral 'wrongs' devouring him are destroyed.

Cohen learns of Brenis's plan: a ritual at his coronation to seize control of the dark power leaking from beneath Svatra into the world, which Cohen and Lacra theorize connects directly to the castle dungeons.

Cohen also confronts a mysterious 'Skull King' entity who calls him a failed half-breed creation of Brenus, offering a bargain Cohen can refuse, and separately helps uncover and end the murderous rampage of the mutated Dr. Simeon, who had been secretly killing people while framing the guilt-ridden vampire Vicho, who ultimately chooses to die at dawn.

Cohen enters a deadly tournament run by the sadistic boyar Bakir, using the alias 'the moth' at the urging of Bakir's abused servant Farcus, wins by brutal means, and ultimately kills Bakir, later denying his ring and giving the cursed amethyst heirloom to Farcus anyway.

Noble conspirator Julen Codrin recruits Cohen to help poison the boyar Ambress before a duel using the dying poison-expert Vera's ritual; Ambress drinks the poisoned blood, is weakened, and killed by Cohen in the duel, with his soul left trapped in Anahora.

Seeking power to face Brenis, Cohen and Anka search for the legendary Font of Life; after passing deadly trials, Cohen alone drinks from it (since there is only enough for one), gaining great strength, and the two become romantically involved.

Having killed two of Brenis's three boyars, Cohen closes in on the last, Zanthy, and continues disrupting Brenis's regime while his reputation as the Verkier-hunting 'Dawnwalker' spreads among the people.

With his infamy at its peak, Brenis offers Cohen a choice of three paths to the endgame: negotiate a trade for his family, join Catalin and the Manummits to break the mountain blockade, or join Lacra to sabotage the coronation ritual directly beneath Svatra.

In the turncoat/negotiation path, Cohen can betray the Manummit hideout to Brenis in exchange for his family and special privileges for Lasa, resulting in the Manummits' massacre and Craig's capture, while Brenis remains in power and the story bypasses a final battle entirely.

In the other routes, Cohen, Lacra, Craig, and Catalin storm Griefberg Castle through a secret passage, finding the dungeons emptied, the desecrated corpse of Kenaz Scander on the throne, and Cohen's family horrifically fused into growths of Anahora's corruption.
Brenis confronts the intruders, mortally wounding Catalin and killing Craig (who sacrifices himself to protect Catalin), before withdrawing to await Cohen with his family.

Lacra destroys the active blood conduit/ritual sphere, believing the risk justified to prevent a greater catastrophe, but this instead causes the barrier between Anahora and reality to collapse uncontrolled around the castle, unleashing undead, spectral horrors, and possession.

Cohen finds his family in the dining hall, missing his sister Luca; he refuses Brenis's offer to spare them if he submits, and the two fight—first in the physical world, then dragged into Anahora itself where Brenis reveals a monstrous true form.

Cohen ultimately defeats Brenis (Francis), who refuses to reveal Luca's fate, having ensured a final cruel joke even in defeat; shortly after, Nebaru/Nebero of the Council of Augers arrives, revealing Lacra and himself serve as Arbiters sent to resolve the crisis.

Cohen learns Luca did not die but was transformed into a Muron by Brenis as a final 'gift'; Nebaru explains she can be guided toward becoming a true Vrair rather than a mindless beast, and gives Cohen a lethal potion/instructions before the pair must leave the valley before winter.

In the epilogue, Cohen reconciles briefly with his catatonic mother Esme and his father Pieta, says goodbye, and departs Veil Sangora with Luca that same night, entering the Council of Augers' service as a Dawnwalker.

In the aftermath, Veil Sangora falls into disorder—its guard disbands, plague returns, gangs rise, the Uryashi retreat to the mountains, and legends of the lone hero who slew Francis begin to spread, while Anka departs to seek a cure for her own corruption and Lacra wanders distant lands evading pursuers.
Long after, a post-credits scene reveals Cohen has survived into the modern era, still fighting as Anahora's corruption begins seeping back into the world.
